46.spine: In 1944 Rajaji offered Jinnah a plebiscite and a weak common centre, and Jinnah took the measure of how far INC would bend. Each later try, the Desai-Liaqat Pact and the Wavell Plan, failed on ML1906's claim to speak for all Muslims, and that claim got stronger after the December 1945 elections. Britain, shaken by QIM, INA agitations and the Naval Mutiny, offered a united India through the Cabinet Mission, but the grouping dispute produced Direct Action Day and a broken Interim Government. By 1947 Atlee fixed a deadline, Mountbatten dropped the idea of unity, INC accepted the 3rd June Plan, and the Indian Independence Act turned partition into law.
beats:
Rajaji meets Jinnah halfway.
Rajagopalachari proposed that ML1906 back Purna Swaraj and join a coalition at the Centre. After the war a plebiscite in Muslim-majority regions would decide on partition, and a yes meant a confederation with a weak centre. INC wanted a Lucknow-Pact-like deal because the British had said no progress without ML1906's consent.
→ But Jinnah wanted far more than a confederation.

Jinnah says no and learns the floor.
Jinnah wanted only Muslims to vote, a fully separate Pakistan (Two Nations, Two States) and all of it before the British left. The talks failed, but Jinnah now knew INC was ready for a Two-Nation, One-State solution. Readiness was INC's compulsion, not its wish.
→ So INC tried again, this time in the Central Assembly.

Desai-Liaqat Pact: parity on paper.
Bhulabhai Desai and Liaqat Ali Khan agreed on a VEC of Indians with 50% INC and 50% ML1906, and 20% of legislature seats for minorities. Gandhi knew of it. Jinnah refused to acknowledge any knowledge of it, testing how far INC could bend.
→ Now the British borrowed this very formula.

Wavell Plan at Shimla.
After the QIM leaders were released, Wavell4347 held the Shimla Conference in June 1945 and proposed a VEC of Indians with 50% Hindus and 50% Muslims. Churchill wanted visible progress before British elections. ML1906 insisted all Muslim ministers be its own; INC said it was not a Hindu party.
→ But the failure itself handed ML1906 a veto and a prize.

December 1945 elections.
Wavell4347 declared failure because ML1906 could not be convinced, an implicit veto at the top. ML1906's prestige soared and it swept the seats reserved for Muslims, winning Bengal and Sindh. INC won elsewhere, including NWFP and Assam, and led a coalition in Punjab.
→ Meanwhile Britain itself was cracking.

Britain exhausted: Cabinet Mission arrives.
Atlee became PM in July 1945, Japan surrendered, the INA trials united Indians, and the Naval Mutiny broke out on the day the Cabinet Mission arrived. Britain no longer trusted the army and was drained by two world wars and the Depression. In March 1946 Atlee said a minority would not be allowed a veto over the majority.
→ So the Mission offered a united India, but with a catch.

Cabinet Mission Plan and the grouping fight.
A weak centre for Defence, Communications and Foreign Affairs, three sections A, B and C, and a Constituent Assembly of PLA members plus princely nominees. INC said grouping was voluntary; ML1906 said it was compulsory, and the British agreed. That made the plan a Pakistan within India.
→ Then INC's July 1946 stand handed Jinnah his trigger.

Direct Action and a broken government.
INC declared NWFP and Assam would not join Groups B and C, and Nehru said only the Constituent Assembly was binding. ML1906 rejected the plan and called Direct Action Day for 16 August 1946; 5,000 died in Calcutta in a week. ML1906 later joined the Interim Government out of fear, took Finance and made it unworkable. The Constituent Assembly met on 9 December 1946 without ML1906.
→ So by early 1947 the British changed course.

Atlee's deadline and Plan Balkan.
In February 1947 Atlee fixed 30 June 1948 for the British exit, with or without a constitution, and Paramountcy was not to pass to any successor. Mountbatten replaced Wavell4347 and came up with Plan Balkan in April 1947, which Nehru killed. Mountbatten concluded that CMP1946 and unity were dead horses, entirely due to Jinnah.
→ So only partition was left on the table.

3rd June Plan and the Radcliffe Line.
INC accepted partition and dominion status in return for a small Pakistan, a strong centre and exit by 15 August 1947. Punjab and Bengal PLAs decided on partition; NWFP, Sylhet, Sindh and Baluchistan voted to join Pakistan. Radcliffe drew the line alone and announced it on 17 August, two days after independence.
→ Then the law and the princes had to be settled.

Independence Act and 565 princes.
The Indian Independence Act of July 1947 gave legal form to the plan and ended Paramountcy over all 565 states. Patel and V.P. Menon brought 552 into India: 549 by accession and J&K, Junagadh and Hyderabad later. The other 13 went to Pakistan.

47.spine: The national movement was a coalition, and each constituency joined on its own terms. Workers entered late, were pulled in at Gaya 1922, and were split by CPI's Comintern-driven swings. Capitalists funded the INM but stopped where capitalism itself was threatened. Dalits and women found the INC useful but built their own platforms (Ambedkar, Periyar, AIWC), while peasants moved from Gandhian protest to AIKS to armed 1946 revolts. Everywhere the INC absorbed rather than represented, and the unfinished business passed to the Republic.
beats:
Workers appear but wait.
Modern industry created workers in the second half of the 19th century. Early unions were welfare bodies (Lokhande 1890) and then the Madras Labour Union (1918). Their strikes had no wider politics.
→ But the INC Moderates saw no reason to take up their cause.

Moderates look away.
Naoroji's 1886 rule kept class issues out of Congress to protect unity with zamindars and Indian industry. Moderates opposed the Factory Acts yet backed workers against British employers (Assam tea 1881-82, GIP Signallers 1899).
→ So Swadeshi, the Extremists and the Russian Revolution had to push labour in.

Labour enters the mainstream.
Swadeshi strikes, the Tilak trial protest and the war-time price rise drew workers in. AITUC (1920) gave an all-India body; C.R. Das at Gaya (1922) argued Congress must absorb class demands or lose them.
→ Now a Left grew inside and outside the INC.

The Left grows and splits.
CPI arrived via Tashkent 1920 and Kanpur 1925 (Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Joshi). The Trade Union Act 1926 recognised unions while Meerut and the 1929 bills coerced them. The 1928 Comintern line made CPI call Congress bourgeois.
→ But 1935 and 1941 turned the line around again.

Capital backs the INM, conditionally.
Colonial tariffs and credit starved Indian business, so FICCI (1927) tied itself to the INC. Business loved Swadeshi, funded Gandhi, cut British cloth imports by half in the CDM and drafted the Bombay Plan, but feared strikes and class war.
→ Meanwhile the INC's silence on caste left Dalits to speak for themselves.

Dalits build their own road.
Walangkar, Vaikom, Periyar's Self-Respect Movement and Guruvayur attacked untouchability. Ambedkar moved to water (Mahad 1927), burnt the Manusmriti and demanded separate electorates.
→ So the 1932 Communal Award forced Gandhi and Ambedkar into direct conflict.

Poona Pact and after.
Gandhi's fast unto death ended with joint electorates and more reserved seats. INC won only half of reserved seats in 1937; Ambedkar's ILP and AISCF were squeezed. After 1946 he drafted the Constitution, quit over the Hindu Code Bill and converted in 1956.
→ Women's story ran in parallel, also without power.

Women: participation without power.
Reformers spoke about women, not with them. Gandhi's frame of sisterhood, charkha and picketing brought millions out, yet INC never made women decision-makers; AIWC (1927) was nationalist first, feminist second.
→ And in the countryside, a Depression turned peasants radical.

Peasants radicalise.
Prices halved 1929-33 but rent and debt did not; CDM politicised the peasantry and the left organised it. AIKS (1936) with Sahajanand and Ranga issued the Kisan Manifesto; Karachi 1931 and Faizpur 1936 tied INC to them.
→ But governing in 1937-39 split INC from the Kisan Sabha.

Ministries, Haripura and war.
INC ministries struck middle-path agrarian deals and used police on Bakasht (about 600 arrests). Haripura 1938 drew a line, AIKS passed to the CPI, and war, famine and Quit India made peasants the backbone of 1942.
→ After 1945 the anger became open revolt.

The 1946 revolts and two readings.
Worli, Bakasht, Punnapra-Vayalar, Tebhaga and Telangana fought feudal extraction, some serving national integration and some outside the Gandhian frame. Chandra reads them as anti-imperial; Bandyopadhyay as autonomous class war.
